notes: Grammar explanations are original project content. Example sentences are harvested at ETL time from the licensed Tanaka corpus; `match` strings are the literal surface forms used for harvesting.

points.title: 〜です
points.summary: Polite copula that turns a noun or na-adjective into a predicate.
points.explanation: です follows a noun or a na-adjective stem and makes the sentence polite. The plain (dictionary) form is だ, and the negative polite form is ではありません / じゃありません. With i-adjectives です is added after the plain form only for politeness (寒いです).
points.formation: N / な-adj stem + です
points.notes: です is not a verb: it does not conjugate for tense beyond でした (past) and ではありません (negative).

points.title: 〜ます
points.summary: Polite present/future verb form used in neutral conversation.
points.explanation: The ます stem (連用形) plus ます forms the polite non-past: 行きます, 食べます. Negation is ません, past is ました, negative past is ませんでした, and the invitation form is ましょう.
points.formation: V-ます stem + ます / ません / ました / ませんでした
points.notes: ます replaces the plain non-past form; it never follows the て form.

points.title: 〜ている
points.summary: Ongoing action, repeated habit, or the state that results from an action.
points.explanation: V-て + いる expresses (a) an action in progress (食べています “is eating”), (b) a habitual action (毎日通っている “goes every day”), or (c) a resulting state (窓が開いている “the window is open”). Motion verbs such as 行く take the resultative reading: 行っている often means “has gone (and is there)”.
points.formation: V-て + いる
points.notes: In casual speech the い is often dropped: 食べてる.

points.title: 〜てください
points.summary: Polite request built on the て form.
points.explanation: V-て + ください asks someone to perform an action. The negative request is ないでください. It is softer than a command (命令形) but still directional, so it is avoided towards superiors in formal settings.
points.formation: V-て + ください / V-ないで + ください
points.notes: For nouns use をお願いします instead of 〜てください.

points.title: 〜たい
points.summary: Expresses the speaker's desire to perform an action.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + たい turns a verb into an i-adjective meaning “want to”. Objects may be marked with を or が. It describes the speaker's inner wish, so it is not used for a third person's desire without がる/そう.
points.formation: V-ます stem + たい（です）/ たくない / たかった
points.notes: For other people's wishes use 〜たがっている.

points.title: 〜が好き
points.summary: Likes and dislikes with the object marked by が.
points.explanation: 好き（な）is a na-adjective meaning “liked”. The thing liked is normally marked with が, not を: 私は音楽が好きです. The opposite is 嫌い（な）, and degrees are given with 大好き / 好きじゃない.
points.formation: N + が + 好き（です）
points.notes: Adding な before a noun: 好きな食べ物.

points.title: 〜から
points.summary: Gives a reason or cause in neutral and casual speech.
points.explanation: から follows the plain or polite form and marks the clause as a reason: 寒いから、窓を閉めます. It is more subjective than ので, so it is the natural choice for requests, refusals and apologies.
points.formation: Plain / polite clause + から
points.notes: Avoid stacking から with ので in formal writing; prefer ので.

patterns.note: reason clause followed by a comma

points.title: 〜けど
points.summary: Casual contrastive conjunction similar to が.
points.explanation: けど (formal: けれども) connects two clauses with a contrastive or softening meaning. It is also used as a sentence-final particle to soften a statement or invite a response.
points.formation: Plain / polite clause + けど / けれども
points.notes: Very common in spoken Japanese; in formal writing use が or しかし.

points.title: 〜ましょう
points.summary: Volitional invitation or offer.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + ましょう invites someone to act together (“let's …”) or offers help (“I'll …”). The plain equivalent is 〜よう / 〜おう.
points.formation: V-ます stem + ましょう / ませんか
points.notes: ませんか is a softer invitation than ましょう.

points.title: 〜ませんか
points.summary: Polite invitation or suggestion.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + ませんか literally asks “won't you?” and functions as a soft invitation. It is less pushy than ましょう and is a standard way to propose plans.
points.formation: V-ます stem + ませんか
points.notes: Do not answer with はい、行きません; answer はい、行きましょう.

points.title: 〜に行く
points.summary: Purpose of movement expressed with に and a motion verb.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + に + 行く/来る/帰る states the purpose of the movement: ご飯を食べに行く. The ます stem behaves like a noun here, so を or へ can also mark the destination.
points.formation: V-ます stem + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る
points.notes: Only verbs of motion can follow the purpose に.

points.title: 〜てから
points.summary: Sequences two actions: the first one happens first.
points.explanation: V-て + から states that the second action follows the completion of the first. The subject of both clauses is normally the same, and the main clause cannot be a command in the strictest usage.
points.formation: V-て + から
points.notes: 〜た後で also means “after”; てから stresses the sequence of the speaker's own actions.

points.title: 〜ので
points.summary: Objective reason, softer and more formal than から.
points.explanation: ので follows the plain form (な before nouns and na-adjectives) and presents a reason as a fact. Because it sounds less demanding it is preferred in requests, explanations and formal speech.
points.formation: Plain form + ので（N / な-adj + な + ので）
points.notes: から is subjective and can end a sentence; ので usually cannot.

points.title: 〜のに
points.summary: Unexpected contrast, often with surprise or complaint.
points.explanation: のに follows the plain form and links two clauses that clash: the second clause is contrary to what the first would lead you to expect. It frequently carries an emotional colour (regret, blame, surprise).
points.formation: Plain form + のに（N / な-adj + な + のに）
points.notes: Do not confuse with the purpose marker 〜のために / 〜ように.

points.title: 〜たら
points.summary: Conditional that treats the first event as completed.
points.explanation: V-た + ら presents the condition as something that will happen or has happened, so the main clause often describes a one-off result, discovery or suggestion: 雨が降ったら行きません.
points.formation: V-た + ら / い-adj かったら / N + だったら
points.notes: Unlike ば, たら can be followed by a volitional or past main clause.

points.title: 〜ば
points.summary: Hypothetical conditional for general cause and effect.
points.explanation: The 仮定形 (e- stem) + ば states a condition: 安ければ買います. Because it is hypothetical it is used for repeated or general consequences, and it cannot normally be followed by a command or an expression of will.
points.formation: V-えば / い-adj ければ / N・な-adj なら(ば)
points.notes: 〜ば〜ほど expresses “the more …, the more …”.

points.title: 〜なら
points.titleEn: if it is the case that …
points.summary: Conditional that takes up the listener's statement as its condition.
points.explanation: なら follows a plain form, noun or na-adjective stem and means “given that …”. It is used when you pick up information you have just heard and add a comment, suggestion or consequence.
points.formation: Plain form / N + なら
points.notes: なら is the only conditional that can follow a noun directly.

points.title: 〜ながら
points.summary: Two actions performed by the same subject at the same time.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + ながら attaches a background action to the main action: 音楽を聞きながら勉強する. The subject of both clauses must be the same.
points.formation: V-ます stem + ながら
points.notes: 〜間に can also mean “while” but allows different subjects.

points.title: 〜ために
points.summary: Purpose (intentional) or cause (unintentional result).
points.explanation: ために has two readings: purpose with an intentional verb in the dictionary form (試験に合格するために勉強する) and cause with a non-intentional verb or noun + の (事故のために遅れた).
points.formation: V-辞書形 + ために / N + の + ために
points.notes: For purpose the verb must be controllable: 雨が降るために is wrong.

points.title: 〜ように
points.titleEn: so that; in such a way that
points.summary: Purpose or goal with non-controllable verbs, and manner.
points.explanation: ように follows the dictionary or potential form for purpose when the verb is not directly controllable (忘れないようにメモする), and the な-adjective form ような / adverbial ように for manner and comparison (彼のように話す).
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ように / N + のように
points.notes: Contrast with ために: ように works with potential and negative verbs.

points.title: 〜てしまう
points.titleEn: to finish completely; to end up (regret)
points.summary: Completion of an action, often with regret or irreversibility.
points.explanation: V-て + しまう marks an action as carried through to the end. With unintentional events it adds a feeling of regret or loss: 財布をなくしてしまった. In casual speech it contracts to 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう.
points.formation: V-て + しまう / ちゃう / じゃう
points.notes: The contracted forms are very common in conversation and are slightly informal.

points.title: 〜ておく
points.summary: Prepare something beforehand or leave a state as it is.
points.explanation: V-て + おく describes doing something in preparation for a later situation (買っておく) or intentionally leaving something in a state (開けておく). Casual form: 〜とく.
points.formation: V-て + おく / とく
points.notes: Often paired with から or あとで to mark the preparation step.

points.title: 〜てみる
points.summary: Attempt an action to see what happens.
points.explanation: V-て + みる means “to try (doing) …” and focuses on the experience rather than the result: 食べてみてください. It is frequently used in the てみる/てみたい/てみてください family.
points.formation: V-て + みる
points.notes: Not used for deliberate trials of ability — use 〜てみせる (show) or 〜ようとする.

points.title: 〜ほうがいい
points.summary: Gives advice or a recommendation.
points.explanation: V-た / V-ない + ほうがいいです recommends a course of action. The negative advice is 〜ないほうがいい. It is advice rather than an order, but it can sound strong towards superiors.
points.formation: V-た + ほうがいい / V-ない + ほうがいい
points.notes: For nouns: N + の + ほうがいい.

points.title: 〜つもり
points.summary: States the speaker's intention or plan.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + つもりです expresses what the speaker plans to do. It is a personal decision and therefore is not normally used for someone else's plan without らしい/そうです.
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + つもり（です）
points.notes: 予定です describes an arrangement; つもり describes an intention.

points.title: 〜なければならない
points.summary: Obligation, with several contracted equivalents.
points.explanation: V-ない stem + なければならない expresses obligation. Common shortenings: なければいけない, なくてはいけない, なきゃ (casual), and the written ねばならない.
points.formation: V-ない stem + なければならない / なくてはいけない / なきゃ
points.notes: With nouns: N + でなければならない.

points.title: 〜てもいい
points.titleEn: may I …? / it is fine to …
points.summary: Gives or asks for permission.
points.explanation: V-て + もいいです grants permission (here: 使ってもいいですよ) and in question form asks for it (撮ってもいいですか). The negative counterpart is 〜なくてもいい (you don't have to).
points.formation: V-て + もいい / V-なくて + もいい
points.notes: 〜てはいけない is the prohibition form.

points.title: 〜てはいけない
points.summary: Prohibition.
points.explanation: V-て + はいけない forbids an action. In conversation it is usually softened to 〜ちゃだめ / 〜てはだめ, and in writing 〜てはならない appears.
points.formation: V-て + はいけない / はだめ / はならない
points.notes: Stronger than 〜ないほうがいい, which is only advice.

points.title: 〜たことがある
points.summary: Past experience.
points.explanation: V-た + ことがある states that the speaker has the experience of doing something at least once. The negative 〜たことがない means “have never”.
points.formation: V-た + ことがある / ことがない
points.notes: Distinguish from 〜こともある (“there are times when …”).

points.title: 〜そうです（伝聞）
points.summary: Hearsay marker attached to the plain form.
points.explanation: Plain form + そうです reports information learned from someone else or the media: 天気予報によると雨だそうです. It is distinct from the conjecture form 〜そう（に見える）which attaches to the ます stem.
points.formation: Plain form + そうです / そうだ
points.notes: Sources are often introduced with によると or では.

points.title: 〜らしい
points.summary: Inference from indirect evidence.
points.explanation: らしい follows the plain form (nouns and na-adjectives without だ) and reports a conclusion drawn from what the speaker has seen or heard. It is more objective than ようだ and keeps some distance from the claim.
points.formation: Plain form + らしい（N / な-adj + らしい）
points.notes: N + らしい also means “typical of N”.

points.title: 〜かもしれない
points.summary: Expresses possibility with uncertainty.
points.explanation: Plain form + かもしれない states that something is possible (roughly 50% or less in the speaker's mind). Casual forms: かもしれない → かも(しれない).
points.formation: Plain form + かもしれない / かも
points.notes: Often paired with もしかすると or ひょっとすると.

points.title: 〜ようになる
points.titleEn: to come to …; to become able to
points.summary: Change of state, habit or ability over time.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / V-ない / potential + ようになる describes a gradual change: 日本語が話せるようになった. With a potential verb it means acquiring an ability; with a plain verb it means that a state or habit has changed.
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない / V-可能形 + ようになる
points.notes: 〜ようにする is the deliberate counterpart (“make an effort to …”).

points.title: 〜ようにする
points.summary: Deliberate attempt to establish a habit.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ようにする means the speaker consciously tries to behave in a certain way: 毎日野菜を食べるようにしている. The 〜ている form stresses the ongoing effort.
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ようにする / ようにしている
points.notes: Contrast with ようになる, which describes change rather than effort.

points.title: 〜ことにする
points.summary: The speaker's own decision.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことにする marks a decision made by the subject: 今年は旅行しないことにした. It focuses on the act of deciding, unlike つもり which reports an intention.
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことにする / ことにしている
points.notes: 〜ことにしている describes a self-imposed rule or habit.

points.title: 〜ことになる
points.summary: Outcome decided by circumstances or other people.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことになる presents a result that follows from a rule, schedule or someone else's decision: 来月から大阪に転勤することになった.
points.formation: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことになる / ことになっている
points.notes: 〜ことになっている describes a rule or arrangement currently in force.

points.title: 〜はず
points.summary: Strong expectation based on evidence or logic.
points.explanation: Plain form + はずです states that something is expected to be the case given what is known: 彼はもう着いているはずです. はずがない denies the expectation (“there is no way …”).
points.formation: Plain form + はず（だ / です）/ はずがない
points.notes: Weaker than a fact, stronger than かもしれない.

points.title: 〜べき
points.summary: Moral or social obligation.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 + べきだ states what one ought to do according to common sense or social norms: 約束は守るべきだ. The negative is 〜べきではない.
points.formation: V-辞書形 + べき（だ）/ べきではない
points.notes: する becomes するべき or すべき; べき only takes the dictionary form.

points.title: 〜わけ
points.summary: Logical conclusion or explanation of a situation.
points.explanation: Plain form + わけだ states that a conclusion follows logically. Common derived forms: わけがない (impossible), わけにはいかない (cannot, for social reasons), わけではない (it is not that …).
points.formation: Plain form + わけだ / わけがない / わけではない / わけにはいかない
points.notes: わけだ draws a conclusion; はずだ expresses an expectation.

points.title: 〜ばかり
points.summary: Emphasises that something happens exclusively or repeatedly.
points.explanation: N / V-て + ばかり limits to one thing (甘い物ばかり食べている) and V-た + ばかり means “just did …”. With 〜んばかり it exaggerates an imminent action.
points.formation: N + ばかり / V-て + ばかりいる / V-た + ばかり
points.notes: 〜だけ is neutral quantity; ばかり adds a subjective nuance of excess.

points.title: 〜しかない
points.summary: Limitation used with a negative predicate.
points.explanation: N / V-辞書形 + しか + negative expresses “only …”: 一つしかない. Unlike だけ, しか always requires a negative verb, and 〜しかない can mean “there is no choice but to …” after a dictionary form.
points.formation: N / V-辞書形 + しか + ない
points.notes: Numbers take しか directly: 三人しか来なかった.

points.title: 〜たびに
points.summary: Repeated occurrence triggered by an event.
points.explanation: V-辞書形 / N + の + たびに states that the main clause happens on each occasion of the trigger: この曲を聞くたびに学生時代を思い出す.
points.formation: V-辞書形 + たびに / N + の + たびに
points.notes: The main clause is normally a state, emotion or habit, not a one-off command.

points.title: 〜うちに
points.summary: Act during a window of time or state.
points.explanation: Plain form (V-ている / V-ない / N + の) + うちに means “while the state lasts”: 明るいうちに帰ろう. It implies the state will change, so the main action should happen inside the window.
points.formation: V-ている / V-ない / い-adj / N + の + うちに
points.notes: 〜間に simply means “during”; うちに adds the nuance “before it is too late”.

points.title: 〜おかげで
points.summary: Positive cause with gratitude.
points.explanation: Plain form / N + の + おかげで attributes a good result to a cause: 先生のおかげで合格した. Used sarcastically it can also blame, but the default is positive.
points.formation: Plain form / N + の + おかげで
points.notes: The negative counterpart is 〜せいで.

points.title: 〜せいで
points.summary: Attributes a bad result to a cause.
points.explanation: Plain form / N + の + せいで assigns responsibility for an undesirable outcome: 雨のせいで試合が中止になった. It carries blame, so it is avoided in polite explanations about the listener.
points.formation: Plain form / N + の + せいで / せいか
points.notes: 〜せいか softens the claim (“maybe because …”).

points.title: 〜ずに
points.summary: Written-style negative accompaniment.
points.explanation: V-ない stem + ずに (する becomes せずに) means “without doing …”: 何も言わずに出て行った. It is the literary equivalent of 〜ないで.
points.formation: V-ない stem + ずに / ず（する → せずに）
points.notes: 〜ず also ends a sentence in formal writing (〜せざるを得ない).

points.title: 〜まま
points.summary: A state is left unchanged.
points.explanation: V-た / V-ない / N + の + まま means the situation stays as it was: 靴のまま上がる, ドアを開けたまま寝てしまった.
points.formation: V-た / V-ない / N + の + まま（で / に）
points.notes: Often appears with にして or で to link clauses.

points.title: 〜ことができる
points.summary: Ability or possibility (potential).
points.explanation: V-辞書形 + ことができる expresses ability or possibility, and is the standard potential form for verbs that have no られる potential: ここから富士山を見ることができる.
points.formation: V-辞書形 + ことができる / ことができない
points.notes: Distinguish ability (できる) from situational possibility (〜られる).

points.title: 〜すぎる
points.summary: Excess in degree or quantity.
points.explanation: V-ます stem / い-adj stem / な-adj stem + すぎる means an action or quality exceeds a reasonable limit: 食べすぎた, 高すぎる. It conjugates as an ichidan verb.
points.formation: V-ます stem / adj stem + すぎる / すぎだ
points.notes: な-adjectives: 静かすぎる (no な).

points.title: 〜やすい / 〜にくい
points.summary: Ease or difficulty of performing an action.
points.explanation: V-ます stem + やすい forms an i-adjective meaning “easy to …”, and にくい means “hard to …”: このペンは書きやすい, この漢字は覚えにくい.
points.formation: V-ます stem + やすい / にくい
points.notes: にくい refers to physical or practical difficulty; がたい is used for psychological difficulty.

points.title: 〜について
points.summary: Topic marker for discussion and thought.
points.explanation: N + について introduces the subject of speech, writing or thought: この問題について話しましょう. The formal written equivalent is 〜に関して.
points.formation: N + について / については / についての + N
points.notes: Not used for physical location — that is 〜に.

points.title: 〜にとって
points.summary: Evaluates something from a standpoint.
points.explanation: N + にとって presents a benchmark or perspective: 私にとって家族が一番大切だ. The following predicate is normally an evaluation (adjective, 重要だ, 難しい), not an action.
points.formation: N + にとって（の + N）
points.notes: 〜に対して means “towards / against”, a different relation.

points.title: 〜に対して
points.summary: Direction of an attitude, or a contrast between two items.
points.explanation: N + に対して marks the target of an action or feeling (先生に対して失礼なことを言った) and is also used to contrast two quantities (日本に対して中国は大きい).
points.formation: N + に対して / に対する + N
points.notes: Written style: 〜に対し. Casual contrast: 〜に比べて.

points.title: 〜として
points.summary: N + として marks a role, capacity or standpoint.
points.explanation: N + として states the capacity in which someone or something acts: 教師として働く, 例として挙げる. With は it becomes としては (“as for …”).
points.formation: N + として / としては / としての + N
points.notes: Do not confuse with 〜にとって (standpoint of evaluation).
